Rename file

    
  

  

    
The packages inside an archive are served from it by its name, so a link already handed out for one of them stops working. An archive keeps its extension.

Delete packages

    
  

  

    
This can't be undone. The files are removed from disk, not moved anywhere — there's no bin to recover them from. 

    

    
    
If something changes inside a folder while it's being deleted (a file appears mid-way through, from another device or a download), the folder is left exactly as it is and the whole delete is reported as failed — but whatever was already removed before that point stays removed. This is rare and only happens if something else writes to the folder at that moment.

    

    

    

    
  




  

    
Unpack leftovers

    
  

  

    
Each of these is what an unpack left half done when it was cut short, in a hidden folder beside its archive. Removing one deletes those files from disk for good; the archive it came from is not touched.

    

    

    

    
  




  

    
Delete archive

    
  

  

    

    
This can't be undone. The files are removed from disk, not moved anywhere — there's no bin to recover them from.

Settings

    
  

  

    
How this instance behaves. Changes take effect at once and are kept in the config folder, and a value saved here wins over the variable it came from; Use the variable hands it back. Items marked container setting need a container change to apply.

    

    

    

      Advanced
      
Settings you rarely need to change. Some are marked "container setting" — those need a change to the container (its Path, Port or Variable entries in Unraid) and a recreate to apply.

      

    

  




  

    
Hide the device root warning

    
  

  

    
The warning is there because a console's device root holds its system partitions. ShadowPKG refuses to rename or delete a folder with a known system name, but that is not a complete guarantee. Once it is hidden, nothing on the page tells you when you are outside the default folder.

    
    

      
      
    

    
Hide for now lasts until this page is reloaded. Hide forever is remembered on this browser; the box under an FTP folder's list turns the warning back on.

  




  

    
Support report

    
  

  

    
What someone helping you would ask for, in one piece: the setup checks, the details behind them and the end of the log. Read it before you copy it. Hiding is best effort: it recognises IP addresses and the names of files and folders, but not console nicknames, host names or game titles, so look through what is left.

    

      
      
    

    
    

      
      
    

  




  

    
Remove console

    
  

  

    

    
It stops being listed here and anything sent to it stops being tracked. The console itself isn't touched, and you can add it back at any time.
